content:
maria: ok team — RFC follow-up. we need a final, pragmatic plan for sunsetting the /v1 public endpoints. proposal: 6-month window, provide a compat proxy + opt-in header, SDK auto-upgrade, and a clear rollback kill-switch. thoughts?

kevin: +1 on the header approach. suggest `X-Redwood-Compat: v1` so we can keep minimal path for old clients. makes routing + metrics easier. :thumbsup:

derek: header works but watch rate-limiting and caching. if we keep v1 logic in the main runtime it increases tail latency for all requests. prefer an isolated proxy layer (small fleet) that rewrites to /v2 and strips header.

lina: SDK owners here — auto-upgrade is doable for the JS/py SDKs but we need an opt-out flag. timeline: we can ship SDK change in 8 weeks, but customers on pinned versions won't get automatic change. docs & changelog required.

sam: recommend a phased rollout:
1) announce + docs + migration guide (2 weeks)
2) launch compat-proxy and header (canary 1% -> 10% -> 50%) (4 weeks)
3) enable SDK auto-upgrade opt-in behind feature flag (2 weeks)
4) 6-month deprecation window with daily telemetry dashboards
add: deprecation banner in Console for orgs using /v1.

kevin: minimal nginx example for the proxy (very small):
```
location /v1/ {
  proxy_set_header X-Redwood-Compat v1;
  proxy_pass https://internal-api/v2/;
}
```
this keeps the runtime untouched. we run the proxy in front of the runtime in a separate ASG.

derek: +1 on separate ASG. add circuit-breaker so heavy v1 clients can't thrash runtime. also capture latency percentiles separately (p50/p90/p99).

sre-bot: deploy queued for compat-proxy small-fleet -> staging at 1769433600 (ETA).

lina: about SDK: we'll add a telemetry ping when SDK switches endpoints so we can enumerate orgs that auto-migrated. also include a migration guide snippet in the SDK repo.

sam: we need a test matrix: end-to-end tests for rewritten paths, canary rollback playbook, and error mismatch tests (v1->v2 differences). assignable to eng-test.

maria: decision time — do we keep a code-path in main runtime as a long-term fallback for emergencies? i worry about complexity.

kevin: we keep a very small emergency passthrough in runtime but guarded by a kill-switch config and strict logging. default is disabled; enable only for customer incident mitigation.

derek: if we do that, add a nightly job that runs a small compatibility smoke test against that runtime path so it doesn't bitrot.

lina: i'll own SDK rollout and migration docs. will coordinate with support for banner copy.

sam: i'll own metrics + canary dashboards; will add alerts for error spike + unexpected traffic on runtime passthrough.

maria: OK — action items:
- lina: SDK changes + docs + support banner (8w)
- kevin: proxy infra + nginx rewrite + rollout plan + kill-switch (4w)
- sam: dashboards + alerts + telemetry (2w)
- derek: circuit-breaker + nightly compatibility smoke tests (3w)
- ops: announce deprecation & timeline (2w)

kevin: one more note — add header `X-Redwood-Compat-Expires: 2026-10-01` on proxy responses so clients see expiry date in their logs.

maria: consensus sounds good. we'll document this as the official sunsetting playbook and schedule a sync with legal + support tomorrow. thanks all. :tada:

deploy-bot: compat-proxy staging deployment started by kevin at 1769433600
